facts.text: Home Plate Formation was deployed at Gusev Crater during Spirit (MER-A) in 2004.

Home Plate is a roughly circular plateau about 80 metres across in the Inner Basin of the Columbia Hills. Spirit found that it was composed of layered rocks with a volcanic origin, likely formed by explosive interaction between magma and water or ice. This was strong evidence for past hydrothermal activity.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Revealed layered volcanic rocks formed by explosive interaction between magma and water or ice — strong evidence for past hydrothermal activity on Mars.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Gusev Crater.
Home Plate is recognised as one of the most scientifically significant geological formations discovered by any Mars rover.
